Section A: questions 1–20 are MCQs (1 mark each); 21–24 have two 1-mark parts; 25–28 have four 1-mark parts; 29 has six 1-mark parts.

Every answer shows the working. Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: The point P with ordinate −3 divides the join of A(6, 5) and B(−1, 4) in the ratio —
questions.work:
Let the ratio be k : 1. y = (4k + 5)/(k + 1) = −3 ⇒ 4k + 5 = −3k − 3 ⇒ k = −8/7.
Negative k means external division in the ratio 8 : 7.

questions.q: The slope of a line which makes 60° with the negative direction of the x-axis is —
questions.work: Angle with the positive x-axis = 180° − 60° = 120°; slope = tan 120° = −√3.

sections.title: Objective type questions of two 1-mark parts.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The eccentricity of 3x² + 4y² = 12 is ______. (b) The length of the major axis of 5x² + 6y² = 3 is ______.
Fill in the blanks: (a) If AX = B has a unique solution, X = ______. (b) A⁻¹ = ______ in terms of adj A.
Fill in the blanks: (a) lim x→1 (x⁴ − 1)/(x − 1) = ______. (b) lim x→0 (e^(2x) − 1)/x = ______.
Fill in the blanks: (a) If y = e^(sin⁻¹x), then dy/dx = ______. (b) d/dx(xˣ) = ______.
questions.answer:
(a) e^(sin⁻¹x) × 1/√(1 − x²).
(b) log y = x log x ⇒ y'/y = log x + 1 ⇒ xˣ(1 + log x).

sections.title: Objective type questions of four 1-mark parts.

questions.q: Answer: (a) Is R = {(1,2), (2,1)} on {1, 2, 3} an equivalence relation? (b) Is f(x) = 3 − 4x on R one-one and onto? (c) If f(x) = 2ˣ, find (f∘f)(0). (d) A binary operation on A is a function from ______ to A.
questions.answer:
(a) No — (1,1) ∉ R, so it is not reflexive (it is also not transitive: (1,2), (2,1) but no (1,1)).
(b) Yes. One-one: 3 − 4a = 3 − 4b ⇒ a = b. Onto: for any y, x = (3 − y)/4 gives f(x) = y.
(c) f(0) = 1, f(1) = 2 ⇒ (f∘f)(0) = 2.
(d) A × A.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) f(x) = x − cos x is ______ for all x. (b) The local minimum of f(x) = 2x³ − 3x² − 12x + 8 is at x = ______. (c) The slope of the normal to x³ + x² + 3xy + y² − 5 = 0 at (1, 1) is ______. (d) The tangent to y = f(x) at (x₁, y₁) is parallel to the x-axis if ______.

Fill in the blanks: (i) The degree of (d²y/dx²)^(1/3) = x is ______. (ii) The differential equation with solution y = a cos x + b sin x is ______. (iii) The solution of dy/dx = e^(x+y) is e^y = ______. (iv) The number of arbitrary constants in a particular solution of a third-order equation is ______.
questions.answer:
(i) Cube both sides: d²y/dx² = x³ ⇒ degree 1.
(ii) y' = −a sin x + b cos x, y'' = −a cos x − b sin x = −y ⇒ y'' + y = 0.
(iii) e^(−y)dy = eˣdx ⇒ −e^(−y) = eˣ + C ⇒ e^y = −1/(eˣ + C).
(iv) 0.

sections.title: Objective type question of six 1-mark parts.

questions.q: f(x) = (1 − x + x²)/(1 + x + x²). (i) How many critical points? (ii) Their signs? (iii) Nature at the positive one? (iv) Nature at the negative one? (v) Local minimum value? (vi) Local maximum value?
questions.answer:
f'(x) = [(−1 + 2x)(1 + x + x²) − (1 − x + x²)(1 + 2x)]/(1 + x + x²)² = 2(x² − 1)/(1 + x + x²)².
(i) f' = 0 at x = ±1: 2 critical points.
(ii) One positive (1), one negative (−1).
(iii) f' changes − to + at x = 1: local minimum.
(iv) f' changes + to − at x = −1: local maximum.
(v) f(1) = 1/3. (vi) f(−1) = 3/1 = 3.

questions.q: Show that |1 a bc; 1 b ca; 1 c ab| = (a − b)(b − c)(c − a).
questions.answer:
R₁ → R₁ − R₂, R₂ → R₂ − R₃:
|0 a−b c(b−a); 0 b−c a(c−b); 1 c ab| = (a − b)(b − c)|0 1 −c; 0 1 −a; 1 c ab|.
Expand along C₁: 1 × (1·(−a) − (−c)·1) = c − a.
So Δ = (a − b)(b − c)(c − a).

questions.q: Solve the matrix equation [[2, −3], [1, 1]][x, y]ᵀ = [1, 3]ᵀ.
If A = {1, 2, 3} and R = {(2, 3)}, check whether R is reflexive, symmetric or transitive.
questions.answer:
Not reflexive: (1,1) ∉ R.
Not symmetric: (2,3) ∈ R but (3,2) ∉ R.
Transitive: there are no pairs (a,b), (b,c) both in R, so the condition holds vacuously.

questions.q: Solve 2tan⁻¹(cos x) = tan⁻¹(2 cosec x).
questions.answer:
2tan⁻¹(cos x) = tan⁻¹[2 cos x/(1 − cos²x)] = tan⁻¹[2 cos x/sin²x].
So 2 cos x/sin²x = 2/sin x ⇒ cos x = sin x ⇒ x = π/4.

questions.q: Evaluate lim x→3 |x − 3|/(x − 3).
questions.answer:
For x > 3 the expression is 1; for x < 3 it is −1.
RHL = 1 ≠ LHL = −1, so the limit does not exist.

questions.q: If y = (x + 1)/(x − 1), x ≠ 1, find d²y/dx².
Differentiate x sin x + cos x with respect to x.
questions.answer: (1·sin x + x cos x) − sin x = x cos x.

questions.q: Find dy/dx for y = x^(x cos x).
questions.answer:
log y = x cos x log x.
(1/y)y' = cos x log x − x sin x log x + cos x.
y' = x^(x cos x)[cos x(1 + log x) − x sin x log x].

questions.q: Show that y = log(1 + x) − 2x/(2 + x), x > −1, is increasing throughout its domain.
Determine a and b so that f(x) = |x − 2|/(x − 2) + a (x < 2), a + b (x = 2), |x − 2|/(x − 2) + b (x > 2) is continuous at x = 2.
If x = a(cos θ + log tan(θ/2)) and y = a sin θ, find d²y/dx².
questions.answer:
dx/dθ = a(−sin θ + 1/sin θ) = a cos²θ/sin θ. dy/dθ = a cos θ.
dy/dx = a cos θ × sin θ/(a cos²θ) = tan θ.
d²y/dx² = sec²θ × dθ/dx = sec²θ × sin θ/(a cos²θ) = sin θ/(a cos⁴θ).

questions.q: Prove that y² = 4x and x² = 4y divide the square bounded by x = 0, x = 4, y = 4 and y = 0 into three equal parts.
questions.answer:
The curves meet at (0, 0) and (4, 4).
Middle part: ∫₀⁴ (2√x − x²/4)dx = [(4/3)x^(3/2) − x³/12]₀⁴ = 32/3 − 16/3 = 16/3.
Lower part (under x² = 4y): ∫₀⁴ x²/4 dx = 16/3.
Upper part = 16 − 16/3 − 16/3 = 16/3. All three are equal.

questions.q: Show that the points with position vectors 4i + 8j + 12k, 2i + 4j + 6k, 3i + 5j + 4k and 5i + 8j + 5k are coplanar.
A dealer has ₹5760 to buy fans (₹360 each) and sewing machines (₹240 each), and space for at most 20 items. Profit is ₹22 per fan and ₹18 per machine. Formulate the LPP and find the maximum profit.
questions.answer:
Maximise Z = 22x + 18y subject to 360x + 240y ≤ 5760 (3x + 2y ≤ 48), x + y ≤ 20, x, y ≥ 0.
Corners: (0, 0), (16, 0), (8, 12), (0, 20).
Z: 0, 352, 176 + 216 = 392, 360.
Maximum profit ₹392 with 8 fans and 12 sewing machines.

questions.q: Show that of all rectangles with a given perimeter, the square has the greatest area.
questions.answer:
Let the perimeter be 2p and the sides x and p − x. Area A = x(p − x) = px − x².
A' = p − 2x = 0 ⇒ x = p/2. A'' = −2 < 0 ⇒ maximum.
Then both sides are p/2: the rectangle is a square.

or.q: Find the point on y² = 4x nearest to (2, 1).
or.answer:
Take the point (t², 2t). D² = (t² − 2)² + (2t − 1)².
d(D²)/dt = 4t(t² − 2) + 4(2t − 1) = 4t³ − 4 = 0 ⇒ t = 1 (second derivative 12t² > 0 ⇒ minimum).
Nearest point: (1, 2).
